info.title: krea/krea-3
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "krea/krea-3", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

example.prompt: A ceramic coffee mug on a clean studio background

aspect_ratio.description: 1:1, 4:5, 3:4, 2:3, 9:16, 5:4, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 or 21:9. Use with resolution; omit for automatic framing.

image_urls.description: Input image URLs, up to 8. Each must be the image_url returned by uploading the image to POST /proxy/krea/assets (multipart form field `file`); any link that is not an https URL on the host app-uploads.krea.ai, including your own https URLs, is rejected with 400, and an app-uploads.krea.ai link that is not a live upload fails with a 5xx error. Omit for text-to-image.

prompt.description: What to generate. With image_urls, the editing instruction; describe what should change and what should stay the same.

regional_edit.description: Set true for a local edit that keeps the rest of the image. Needs model berry and at least one image in image_urls.

thinking_mode.description: fast (default), high or ultra. High and ultra plan complex edits in more detail and take longer. Ultra needs resolution 2k.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

result.description: The finished generation. Not nullable here, unlike on `KreaJob`: a terminal job whose `result` carries no `urls` is answered as a Comfy Router error, so a `200` always carries it.

style_id.description: Set by loraTraining jobs rather than by a generation; a `200` for these models carries `urls`.

urls.description: The generated images, as downloadable links. At least one, because a `completed` job with an empty `urls` is `success_without_output` and never reaches this document.

status.description: Always `completed` on this document: it is the only status Router reports as a success, and Krea's vocabulary is matched without a case fold.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Krea 2 and Krea 3 image models: the terminal `GET /proxy/krea/jobs/{job_id}` job document, forwarded unchanged. Every Krea generate operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/krea/generate/image/krea/krea-2/{size}` answers with this same `KreaJob` document in a NOT-YET-FINISHED state (a `job_id`, a pending `status`, a null `result`), and Router makes that submit and then polls `GET /proxy/krea/jobs/{job_id}` on the caller's behalf for all three size operations, applying the terminal-state rule below. So the body a caller receives is the finished job rather than that pending handle. The three sizes — medium, medium-turbo and large — share one status route and this one document shape, and `krea/krea-2` resolves to the same medium operation `krea/krea-2-medium` does.
The generated images are at `result.urls[]`, an array of downloadable links. `result` is null until the job finishes, and a caller must key completion off `result.urls` rather than off `result` being present: `KreaJobResult`'s other field, `style_id`, is what a loraTraining job returns, so a `result` carrying only a style id is a job that generated no image. Router draws the same line — a `completed` whose `result.urls` is empty is `success_without_output`, not a finished generation.
`status` is Krea's own lowercase nine-value vocabulary — `backlogged`, `queued`, `scheduled`, `processing`, `sampling`, `intermediate-complete`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` — forwarded unchanged and compared without a case fold. `completed` is the only terminal SUCCESS. `intermediate-complete` reads like a terminal state and is not: it is a partial preview of a generation that is still running, and polling continues through it — treating it as finished would return a preview as the result. `failed` and `cancelled` are both terminal FAILURES; a cancelled job is one the provider stopped, not a success that produced nothing. Through Router that distinction is already settled, because a terminal job carrying no `result.urls` is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with the provider document.
The composition NARROWS `KreaJob` rather than republishing it, because `KreaJob` describes every poll of the job — including the pending ones the caller never sees — while this document describes only the body a `200` carries. Router reports success on exactly one shape: `status` `completed` AND a `result.urls` with at least one non-empty entry. A still-running status is polled again rather than returned, and every other terminal reading is a Comfy Router error rather than this document, so `status` is narrowed to the single terminal success and `result` is required non-null with a non-empty `urls`. Left unnarrowed, the schema would publish `intermediate-complete` with a null `result` as a valid `200` — the preview-as-result outcome the paragraph above says Router forbids — and a generated client would type the finished asset as optional. Narrowing `status` here is safe in a way it is NOT for BFL (see `BFLRouterResultOutput`, which declines the same narrowing): Krea's vocabulary is compared WITHOUT a case fold, so `completed` is the only spelling that can reach a `200`. `minItems: 1` and not a per-item `minLength`, because Router's rule is that at least ONE element is non-empty, not that every one is.

status.description: Available options: backlogged, queued, scheduled, processing, sampling, intermediate-complete, completed, failed, cancelled
